blind.why: Character lineup (gal_lineup vs ss_1). CS2 agents shoulder their weapons with weight shifted and distinct silhouettes. Ours all stand in the same 'chicken-wing' hold: upper arms near horizontal, the support arm laid flat across the chest, a toy-sized rifle held at sternum height, the head sunk between the shoulder pads, and identical rigid legs.

In the map at 5 to 15 m (map_lineup vs t2_028). The CS2 player reads instantly as one silhouette with the weapon up. Ours is readable at 5 m, but at 15 m both the Ember and the Tide figure are dark navy with magenta or cyan holo trim and wings, so I could not tell the teams apart. The pistols are invisible specks.

Shaded arcade at about 20 m (m2_reverse vs t4_005). The CS2 T model has clean figure-ground contrast. Ours has gold back-wing cosmetics that double the silhouette width and hide the arms and weapon, and both teams use black/white or gold prison stripes.

biggest_gap: Cosmetics override team identity. Resolved cosmetic specs ignore the team, and in shots/critic-avatars/m4.json actor 3 (ember) and actor 4 (tide) have byte-identical specs (suit base #1a0b3d, magenta #ff2cd6 accent, holo circuit pattern, antenna helmet). Repro: in ?test=1&seed=1, push 10 createActor() actors 20 m down the Tide Spawn sightline (pos 4,0,-46.8, yaw 3.054). At 15 to 20 m about half the roster reads as dark purple/magenta and you cannot tell Ember from Tide; wings and horn/halo helmets also change the silhouette. CS2 keeps the team readable through a fixed T/CT model family and silhouette, and skins never change team read. Fix: lock the suit's dominant hue/value to the team (cosmetics may only tint within an orange or teal band and set the pattern), force a bright team-coloured emissive band visible from every angle, and cap back items and helmets to a fixed silhouette envelope.
other_gaps: Headshots register as chest. The chest capsule (chest bone +0.25, r 0.235) reaches about 1.71 m and swallows the lower head and visor. Ray grid against the skinned mesh: 36 to 46 of about 100 mesh hits above 1.5 m report hitgroup 'chest'. Capsules overall have IoU 0.72 to 0.85 against the mesh, with 0.11 to 0.16 m^2 of phantom hit area per actor (crouch is worst). Shrink and lower the chest capsule and make the head win ties.

Hold and aim poses: every weapon class (smg, rifle, sniper, shotgun, lmg) uses the same flat-elbow chest hug with no shouldering and no cheek weld, and the held taggers are about half scale. CS2 third-person shoulders rifles with the support arm extended under the barrel.

Reload is almost invisible in third person: over 2 s only the left hand drifts about 10 cm. There is no gun tilt, no mag-out or mag-in beat and no body motion. Throw showed no readable wind-up in a 1 s sample.
Tag-out: the shatter frame adds a huge over-exposed white/pink ground disc (seq_tagout frames 3 to 5) that reads like a bloom bug. The held tagger stays un-frozen and floats during the freeze.
Crouch-walk feet lift only 4 cm (foot y 0.070 to 0.113), which reads as shuffling. The crouch silhouette goes almost black in shade, and team colour is lost.

Draw calls: render.info calls went from 207 to 367 when 10 actors were added (about 16 per actor including shadow and held tagger), not 'one draw call each'. CPU is fine: characters.update takes 0.55 ms for 10 actors.
bugs: Cross-team identical cosmetic specs (actor ids 3 and 4 in m4.json) make Ember and Tide indistinguishable
Head/visor shots resolve to the chest hitgroup (chest capsule overlaps the head sphere)
Hitbox debug overlay draws the hidden first-person view actor's capsules as screen-spanning lines (m2_hitbox.png)
strengths: Default orange and teal kits are clean, chunky and very readable at 5 to 30 m in sun
Run and walk foot planting is solid: mean planted-foot slide is 3 to 4 cm/s
The run cycle has a convincing stride and arm swing
Freeze-to-crystal then confetti shatter reads well and suits the tag-sport tone
No console errors; the animation cost is cheap
